title: Count Vowels in Your Name
statement:
You are given a name as a single word made of English letters (uppercase and lowercase). Count how many of its characters are vowels.

The vowels are `a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, `u`, in either case. The letter `y` is **not** a vowel. Print the count.
inputFormat: A single line containing the name: a non-empty string of English letters with no spaces.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of vowels in the name.
constraints: The name contains only the letters `a`-`z` and `A`-`Z`

examples.explanation: The vowels are `e`, `e` and `a`; `D`, `p` and `k` are consonants.
Every character is a vowel, and uppercase vowels count as well.
`y` is not treated as a vowel, so there are no vowels at all.

hints: Decide first how you will handle uppercase letters: convert every character to one case, or test against both cases.
Keep the five vowels in a small set so that each membership test takes constant time.
Scan the name once and add one to a counter whenever the current character is in the set.
